abstract: Maintains operational robotics technical staffing and subsea tooling allocations
system_message:
You are Subsea Robotics Engineering Lead (SREL). The Subsea Robotics Engineering Lead (SREL) maintains operational robotics technical staffing and subsea tooling allocations, tracking crew counts across operational shifts as well as umbilical telemetry performance for subsea search taskforces.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Umbilical fiber-optic telemetry（TEL）
information_points.content:
SREL-TEL-EVN：Bench testing of the main umbilical optoelectronic cores for the Tethered Heavy-Workclass ROV Survey measures a sustained telemetry uplink bandwidth of 10 Gbps to the topside command cabin.
SREL-TEL-S4B：Bench testing of the main umbilical optoelectronic cores for the Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Swarm Deployment confirms a sustained telemetry uplink bandwidth of 1 Gbps from the subsea frame to the topside command cabin.
SREL-TEL-Z9N：Bench testing of the main umbilical optoelectronic cores for the Deep-Towed Synthetic Aperture Sonar Transect records a sustained telemetry uplink bandwidth of 5 Gbps to the topside command cabin.

information_points.title: Maintains operational robotics technical staffing and subsea tooling allocations（ROBOT）
information_points.content:
SREL-ROBOT-NF5：For the Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Swarm Deployment, the count of subsea robotics technical specialists dedicated to continuous vehicle maintenance, launch, and recovery shifts is 12 persons under the staffing accounting basis including standby relief personnel.
SREL-ROBOT-6UX：For the Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Swarm Deployment, the shift schedule records 14 persons as subsea robotics technical specialists when evaluated under the staffing accounting basis excluding standby relief personnel.
SREL-ROBOT-Y0R：For the Tethered Heavy-Workclass ROV Survey, operational shifts account for 8 persons as subsea robotics technical specialists when calculated including standby relief personnel.
SREL-ROBOT-7VQ：For the Deep-Towed Synthetic Aperture Sonar Transect, the subsea robotics technical specialists staffing schedule allocates 14 persons across continuous operations shifts, determined on the basis including standby relief personnel.
